examples.en: The heel of my shoe came off, so it was hard to walk.

examples.ko: 뒷굽이 너무 높은 신발은 발이 아파요.
examples.en: Shoes with very high heels hurt my feet.

examples.ko: 신발 뒷굽을 새로 갈아 달라고 했어요.
examples.en: I asked them to replace the heel of my shoes.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날 뒷굽이 미끄러워서 넘어질 뻔했어요.
examples.en: The heels were slippery on a rainy day and I almost fell.

examples.ko: 이 운동화는 뒷굽에 쿠션이 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: These sneakers are comfortable because there's cushioning in the heel.
I left my worn-heeled shoes at the repair shop.

explain: 신발 뒤쪽 바닥에 붙은 높은 부분이에요. 그냥 '굽'이라고도 해서 '굽이 높다'처럼 말해요. 신발 뒤쪽 전체를 말할 때는 '뒤축'을 써요.

phrases.en: The heels of my dress shoes were worn, so I had them repaired.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신발을 오래 신으면 닳는 부분이라 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pair, since heels wear down with long use.

phrases.en: Shoes with low heels are comfortable.
phrases.nuance_ko: 굽의 높이를 말할 때는 '높다/낮다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 높다 or 낮다 to describe how tall the heel is.

phrases.en: The heels are high, so I can't walk for long.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒷굽'을 줄여서 '굽'이라고도 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: People often shorten 뒷굽 to just 굽.

explain_en: It is the raised part attached to the bottom back of a shoe. People also just say '굽', as in '굽이 높다'. When talking about the whole back part of the shoe, '뒤축' is used.

examples.en: You have to wear protective glasses during experiments.
Protective glasses protect your eyes.
At a construction site, protective glasses are a must.
Welding without protective glasses is dangerous.
I kept out the dust with protective glasses.
I bought a pair of protective glasses for kids.

explain: 먼지, 불꽃, 약품 같은 것에서 눈을 지키려고 쓰는 안경이에요. '쓰다'와 같이 쓰고, 실험실이나 공사장 안내문에서 자주 보여요. 눈이 나빠서 쓰는 일반 '안경'과는 목적이 달라요.

phrases.en: Please wear protective glasses when you work.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안경을 얼굴에 쓸 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for putting glasses on your face.

phrases.en: You must wear safety goggles in the lab.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보호안경'을 줄인 말이고, 안내문에서 많이 보여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 보호안경, seen often on signs.

phrases.en: Bring protective glasses when you go to the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미리 준비해서 가져간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to prepare and bring them in advance.

explain_en: They are glasses worn to protect the eyes from dust, sparks or chemicals. Use it with '쓰다', and you often see it on lab or construction-site notices. The purpose differs from ordinary '안경' worn for poor eyesight.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 거동이 불편하셔서 의사 선생님이 왕진을 오셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather has trouble moving around, so the doctor came to make a house call.
Does this clinic also make house calls?

examples.ko: 의사 선생님은 눈 오는 날에도 왕진을 갔어요.
examples.en: The doctor went on a house call even on a snowy day.

examples.ko: 왕진 요청 전화를 받고 의사가 서둘러 나갔어요.
examples.en: After receiving a call asking for a house call, the doctor hurried out.

examples.ko: 왕진 가방을 들고 의사 선생님이 들어오셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor came in carrying a house-call bag.
Where should I call to request a house call?

explain: 의사가 환자의 집으로 찾아가서 진료하는 것이에요. 의사가 가는 쪽은 '왕진을 가다', 환자 쪽에서 보면 '왕진을 오다'라고 해요. 요즘 말로는 '방문 진료'라고도 해요.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님이 환자 집으로 왕진을 가셨어요.
phrases.en: The doctor went to the patient's home for a house call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 의사 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the doctor's point of view.

phrases.example: 할머니 댁에 의사 선생님이 왕진을 오셨어요.
phrases.en: The doctor came to Grandmother's house for a house call.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자 쪽에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the patient's point of view.
phrases.en_equiv: the doctor comes for a house call

phrases.example: 요즘은 방문 진료를 해 주는 병원이 있어요.
phrases.en: These days some clinics offer home-visit care.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 요즘에는 이 말을 더 자주 들어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and it is heard more often these days.

explain_en: It is when a doctor goes to the patient's home to give treatment. The doctor 'goes' (왕진을 가다), and from the patient's side the doctor 'comes' (왕진을 오다). Another current term is '방문 진료'.

examples.en: The doctor examined the patient slowly.
This clinic sees patients on Sundays too.

examples.ko: 오늘은 오후 다섯 시까지만 진료할 거예요.
examples.en: Today we will see patients only until five in the afternoon.
The child did not cry during the examination.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 먼저 진료하고 약을 지어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor examined me first and then prepared the medicine.

examples.ko: 휴가 때문에 병원이 이틀 동안 진료하지 않아요.
examples.en: The clinic will not see patients for two days because of a holiday.

explain: 주어는 보통 의사나 병원이에요. 환자는 '진료를 받다'라고 말해요. '치료하다'는 병을 낫게 하는 일이고, '진료하다'는 보고 검사하고 진단하는 것까지 넓게 가리켜요.

phrases.en: I got a medical examination at the hospital yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환자의 입장에서 말할 때 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural way to speak from the patient's side.

phrases.en: Please check the hospital's consultation hours.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원이 환자를 보는 시간을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The hours when a hospital sees patients.

phrases.en: I made an appointment for tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에 미리 시간을 잡을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when booking a time with a hospital in advance.

explain_en: A doctor sees patients at a clinic; medical setting. The subject is usually a doctor or a clinic; the patient says '진료를 받다'. 치료하다 is about curing an illness, while 진료하다 covers examining and diagnosing as well.

dis.h: a doctor sees and treats patients
gh: give medical care to cure an illness
heal, especially wounds of the heart
give quick first-aid care on the spot

p.n: 치료하다 focuses on curing; 진료하다 on the visit and exam.

t90.ax: The doctor examined the patient slowly.

examples.en: I carefully pulled out the splinter with tweezers.
Could you lend me tweezers?
I bought tweezers to shape my eyebrows.
I had no tweezers, so I picked it up with chopsticks.
The tips of the tweezers are sharp, so be careful.

examples.ko: 핀셋은 화장품 가게에서 쉽게 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can easily buy tweezers at a cosmetics shop.

explain: 작은 것을 집는 도구인데, 뉴스에서는 '핀셋 지원, 핀셋 규제'처럼 필요한 곳만 정확히 골라 한다는 비유로도 많이 써요. 이런 때는 도구가 아니라 방식을 말하는 거예요.

phrases.example: 정부가 피해가 큰 업종에만 핀셋 지원을 하기로 했어요.
phrases.en: The government decided to give targeted support only to the hardest-hit industries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넓게 퍼뜨리지 않고 필요한 대상만 골라 정확히 한다는 뜻이에요. 주로 뉴스에서 지원, 규제, 방역 같은 말과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means choosing only the needed targets instead of spreading widely. It is mainly used in the news with words like support, regulation and quarantine.

explain_en: It is a tool for picking up small things, but in the news it is also used figuratively, as in '핀셋 지원' and '핀셋 규제', to mean targeting only exactly the needed spots. In those cases it describes a method, not the tool.

en: thoracic surgery; department of thoracic surgery

examples.en: You get heart surgery at the thoracic surgery department.

examples.ko: 저희 아버지는 큰 병원 흉부외과 의사세요.
examples.en: My father is a doctor in the thoracic surgery department of a big hospital.
I have a problem with my lung, so I went to thoracic surgery.
The thoracic surgery department at our hospital is always busy.

examples.ko: 이 병원에는 흉부외과 전문의가 세 분 계세요.
examples.en: This hospital has three thoracic surgery specialists.

examples.ko: 내과 의사가 저를 흉부외과에 소개해 줬어요.
examples.en: The internal medicine doctor referred me to thoracic surgery.

explain: 약으로 치료하는 '내과'와 달리, 수술이 필요한 가슴 쪽 문제를 맡는 과예요. 심장이나 폐가 아파도 처음에는 내과에서 진찰받고, 수술이 필요할 때 흉부외과로 이어지는 경우가 많아요. '정형외과', '신경외과'처럼 '~외과' 이름과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 흉부외과 의사가 수술 방법을 설명해 줬어요.
phrases.en: The thoracic surgeon explained the surgery method.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과 이름 뒤에 '의사'를 붙여 담당 의사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '의사' after the department name refers to the doctor.

phrases.en: I booked a thoracic surgery appointment for tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병원에서 진료를 예약하거나 받을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when booking or receiving care at a hospital.

phrases.en: The hospital told me to go to thoracic surgery.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 과에서 이 과로 넘어가는 상황에서 '-(으)로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '-(으)로' when being referred from another department.

explain_en: Unlike '내과' (internal medicine), which mostly treats with medicine, this department handles surgery on the chest area. Even for heart or lung trouble, many people first see internal medicine and are sent to thoracic surgery when an operation is needed. It helps to learn it with other '~외과' names like '정형외과' and '신경외과'.

examples.en: I have something important to ask of you.
I have something important to tell you, teacher.

examples.ko: 친구가 긴히 상의할 게 있다고 전화했어요.
examples.en: A friend called to say he had something important to discuss.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁에 긴히 의논할 일이 있는데 시간 돼요?
examples.en: I have something important to discuss tonight; do you have time?

examples.ko: 그분이 긴히 찾으신다고 하니 가 보세요.
examples.en: He says he urgently wants to see you, so please go.

examples.ko: 긴히 할 얘기가 있다고 해서 따로 만났어요.
examples.en: He said he had something serious to say, so we met privately.

explain: 부탁, 말씀, 상의, 의논 같은 말 앞에서 '중요하고 급한 일이 있다'는 느낌을 줘요. 조금 격식 있고 약간 옛스러운 말투라서 일상에서는 '급하게', '꼭'을 쓰기도 해요. 주로 '긴히 부탁할 게 있어요' 같은 표현으로 나와요.

phrases.en: I called because I have an important favor to ask.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 쓰임으로, 중요한 부탁을 조심스럽게 꺼낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common use, for carefully raising an important request.

phrases.example: 긴히 할 말이 있는데 잠깐 시간 되세요?
phrases.en: I have something important to say. Do you have a moment?
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 이야기를 시작하기 전에 상대의 주의를 끌 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to get someone's attention before an important talk.
phrases.en_equiv: to have something important to say

phrases.en: Something came up that I need to discuss seriously with my parents.
phrases.nuance_ko: 중요한 일을 따로 이야기해야 할 때 써요. 조금 격식 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an important matter needs a private talk; somewhat formal.

explain_en: Formal, polite; for a private, important request to someone (긴히 부탁하다) Before words like request, remark, consultation and discussion, it gives the feeling that something important and pressing is coming. It sounds a bit formal and slightly old-fashioned, so in daily talk people may use '급하게' or '꼭' instead. It mostly appears in phrases like '긴히 부탁할 게 있어요'.

examples.ko: 할머니가 병원에 가실 때 제가 동행했어요.
examples.en: I accompanied my grandmother when she went to the hospital.
The team leader will go along on the business trip.

examples.ko: 아이는 보호자와 동행해야 들어갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: Children can only enter if accompanied by a guardian.

examples.ko: 길을 모르는 친구와 동행해서 목적지까지 갔어요.
examples.en: I went with a friend who didn't know the way, all the way to the destination.
The reporter covered the players while traveling with them.
I want to keep walking together with you for a long time.

explain: 동행하다는 어떤 곳에 같이 갈 때 쓰는 격식 있는 말이에요. '같이 가다'가 일상 표현이라면 동행하다는 공식적인 자리나 글, 안내문에서 더 자주 나와요. 비유로 인생을 함께 걷는다는 느낌으로도 써요.

phrases.en: Let's go to the hospital together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '동행하다' 대신 쉬운 '같이 가다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily talk, the easier '같이 가다' is used instead of '동행하다'.

phrases.en: Please accompany them as their guardian.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 주세요'를 붙여 공식적인 자리에서 함께 가 달라고 부탁해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-아/어 주세요' you politely ask someone to come along in a formal setting.

phrases.example: 동행자는 한 명만 들어갈 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Only one companion can go in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 가는 사람을 안내문에서 부르는 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal word used on notices for the person who goes along.

explain_en: A person goes along with another, on a trip or errand. 동행하다 is a formal word for going somewhere together. '같이 가다' is the everyday phrase, while 동행하다 appears more in official situations, writing, and notices. It can also be used figuratively for walking through life together.

t90.ax: The team leader will go along on the business trip.

examples.en: I gladly accepted the invitation.
I accepted my friend's request and helped with the move.
Will you accept this offer?
I am thinking about whether to accept the company's terms.
I accepted the apology and we made up.

examples.ko: 입사 제안을 수락하는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took me a day to accept the job offer.

explain: 수락하다는 부탁·제안·초대 같은 상대의 요청을 받아들일 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '좋아요', '알겠어요'라고 하고, 수락하다는 글이나 공식적인 자리에서 더 자주 나와요. 반대말은 '거절하다'예요.

phrases.en: I accepted the company's offer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 계약 같은 공식적인 제안을 받아들일 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for accepting formal offers such as jobs or contracts.

phrases.en: My friend accepted my apology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수락하다보다 일상적이고 마음으로 받아 준다는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 수락하다, with a feeling of accepting something in your heart.

phrases.en: I won't accept those terms.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받아들이지 않겠다고 분명히 말할 때 써요. 반대말은 '거절하다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to clearly say you won't agree; the opposite word is 거절하다.

explain_en: Neutral and common; accepting requests, offers, or proposals in daily life. 수락하다 is for accepting a request, offer, or invitation. In casual talk people just say '좋아요' or '알겠어요'; 수락하다 appears more in writing and formal settings. The opposite is '거절하다'.

en: to understand; to excuse; to bear with

examples.ko: 늦어서 죄송한데 한 번만 양해해 주세요.
examples.en: I'm sorry I'm late, so please bear with me just this once.
When I explained the situation, everyone understood.
The construction is noisy, so we would appreciate your understanding.

examples.ko: 손님이 사정을 양해해 줘서 환불 없이 넘어갔어요.
examples.en: The customer understood and let it pass, so no refund was needed.

examples.ko: 선생님이 사정을 양해하고 시간을 더 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher understood my situation and gave me more time.
It was agreed on in advance, so there was no problem.

explain: '이해하다'는 내용을 아는 것이고, 양해하다는 불편이나 실수를 알고도 넘어가 주는 쪽이에요. '양해해 주세요', '양해를 구하다'처럼 부탁하거나 안내할 때 거의 이 틀로 써요.

phrases.en: I asked the customer for their understanding first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불편을 주기 전에 이해해 달라고 부탁하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Asking for someone's understanding before causing an inconvenience.

phrases.en: There's construction going on and it's noisy. Thank you for your understanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 안내문이나 가게에서 정중하게 부탁할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Commonly used on notices or in shops as a polite request.

phrases.example: 기다려 주셔서, 또 양해해 주셔서 감사해요.
phrases.en: Thank you for waiting and for your understanding.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불편을 넘어가 준 사람에게 고마움을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to thank someone who let a problem pass.

explain_en: Polite request, ask someone to bear with you (양해해 주세요) '이해하다' is grasping the content; 양해하다 is knowing about an inconvenience or mistake and letting it pass. It mostly appears in set phrases like '양해해 주세요' and '양해를 구하다' when asking or announcing.

gh: understand spoken words, catch what's said
understand; general, comprehend meaning or feelings

p.n: 양해하다 politely asks someone to excuse or allow something and is more formal; 이해하다 asks for understanding.

t90.ax: When I explained the situation, everyone understood.

en: to consent; to accept; to grant

examples.en: The department head gladly agreed to my request.
After thinking for a long time, he agreed to the marriage.
Check the conditions before you accept the offer.

examples.ko: 부모님이 응낙하시면 여행을 갈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If my parents agree, I can go on the trip.

examples.ko: 그녀는 바로 응낙하지 않고 생각해 보겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: She didn't agree right away and said she would think about it.

examples.ko: 상대가 응낙해서 계약을 맺을 수 있었어요.
examples.en: The other side agreed, so we were able to sign the contract.

explain: 부탁이나 제안을 받아들인다는 격식 있는 말이에요. 말할 때는 보통 '허락하다', '승낙하다', '받아들이다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 글이나 이야기 속에서 이 말을 볼 수 있어요. 윗사람이 허락할 때는 '응낙하시다'처럼 높여요.

phrases.example: 선생님이 제 부탁을 흔쾌히 응낙해 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My teacher gladly agreed to my request.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기꺼이 받아들인다는 느낌이라 가장 자연스러운 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most natural pairing, conveying willing acceptance.

phrases.example: 그는 제 제안을 끝내 응낙하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He never accepted my proposal in the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 제안을 받아들이지 않았다는 뜻으로, 부정형으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning a request or proposal was not accepted.

phrases.en: The president accepted our proposal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 받아들였을 때는 '-시-'를 넣어 높여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When a superior agrees, '-시-' is added to show respect.

explain_en: Formal, literary; usually a superior or authority granting a request. It is a formal word for accepting a request or proposal. In speech people usually say '허락하다', '승낙하다' or '받아들이다', and you are more likely to see this word in writing or stories. When a superior agrees, you honor them as '응낙하시다'.

t90.ax: If my parents agree, I can go on the trip.

examples.en: The elevator buttons have braille, so they are convenient.
Visually impaired people read the braille in books with their fingers.
This children's book is also made in braille.

examples.ko: 길바닥의 점자 블록은 안전한 길을 알려 줘요.
examples.en: The tactile paving on the ground shows a safe path.
I heard that braille is not hard to learn.
The medicine box has a braille mark.

explain: '점자를 읽다/배우다'처럼 쓰고, 눈으로 보는 게 아니라 손으로 읽어요. 길바닥에 깔린 '점자 블록', 책인 '점자책'처럼 생활 속에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I borrowed a braille book from the library.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점자로 만든 책을 한 단어로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for a book made in braille.

phrases.example: 길에 있는 점자 블록 위에는 물건을 놓지 마세요.
phrases.en: Please don't put things on the braille blocks on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시각장애인이 길을 찾도록 바닥에 깐 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the blocks laid on the ground to guide visually impaired people.

phrases.en: That child reads braille with their fingertips.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점자는 눈이 아니라 손으로 읽는다는 점이 드러나는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation showing that braille is read by hand, not by eye.

explain_en: It is used as in '점자를 읽다/배우다', and it is read by touch, not by sight. You see it often in daily life, such as '점자 블록' (tactile paving) on the ground and '점자책' (braille books).
